name: substrate-divergence-counterfactual
title: Mechanics-dominated counterfactual (positive control)
claim: RE-RUN 2026-11-05 (reviewer: "auto-reconnect isn't working here"). Reconnect WAS on; it is now also faster (merged 4-way vertices detach at p_4 = 1 per unit time instead of 0.1, T1 at 0.2 x side), and the playback's vertex panel counts neighbour exchanges frame by frame. In this regime the vertex run still makes only 3 exchanges in 80 steps (vs 74 in the Sego run): with 15 A cells (nearly all on the border) and a one-row B stripe, nothing shrinks a junction to the T1 threshold, so the vertex clusters keep their topology while the CPM blobs flow -- the substrate difference this control is built to expose, not a disabled reconnect. Equivalence is still REJECTED (same 0.775, cross 0.450, Delta +0.325 vs +/-0.10). Earlier reading (2026-10-28): In a MECHANICS-DOMINATED regime (strong differential adhesion + a strong chemoattractant gradient, no shared rules/ODE), the spatial equivalence test still REJECTS equivalence after the 2026-10-28 vertex revision. Cross-backend spatial agreement is 0.417 vs same-backend 0.775 (diff +0.358 > margin 0.10), now with mechanics-stochastic replicates, so the same-backend baseline is a genuine stochastic null rather than 1.0 by construction. It remains the POSITIVE CONTROL: the same test that finds the Sego model fate-equivalent detects a substrate difference here. REVISED MECHANISM: the earlier attribution (vertex A cells climbing the gradient to y~17.9 while CPM stays at ~10.7) was an artifact of the old uncalibrated vertex chemotaxis. With chemotactic drift calibrated to the CPM (saturating), neither substrate moves A far (CPM mean y 11.0 -> 11.0, vertex 10.7 -> 10.1). The divergence is now positional / sorting dynamics, not migration direction, and is not yet causally isolated.
experiment: Run a mechanics-only blueprint (workspace/blueprints/mechanics_divergence.yaml: types A/B, A self-adhesive and repelled by B, a chemo field secreted by B with strong chemotaxis on A) on BOTH backends over rules-seeds {0,1,2} (N=80). Score the same-backend and cross-backend exact-position spatial agreement and apply the SAME metrics.equivalence_tost used by crossparadigm-equivalence (margin +/-0.10).
result: 2026-11-05: spatial same 0.775, cross 0.450, TOST Delta +0.325 (pair CI [+0.116, +0.534]), outside +/-0.10 -> NOT equivalent; vertex neighbour exchanges 3 over 80 steps. Superseded 2026-10-28 result: Spatial agreement (N=80, seeds {0,1,2}, mechanics seeded per replicate): same-backend 0.775, cross-backend 0.417; TOST diff +0.358, outside +/-0.10 -> NOT equivalent. Type-A mean y: CPM 11.0 -> 11.0 (seeds 10.7 / 10.1 / 12.2); vertex 10.7 -> 10.1 (10.4 / 9.9 / 10.0). The large directed-migration difference reported earlier no longer appears once the vertex chemotaxis is calibrated to the CPM's saturating drift.

purpose.question: When MECHANICS (not the shared mechanism) drives the outcome, does the equivalence test correctly REJECT -- i.e. does it have the power to detect a real substrate difference?
purpose.mechanism: CPM moves cells by Metropolis acceptance of lattice copies (chemotaxis as an energy bias); the vertex fork moves them by the ActiveMigration director sampled from the field gradient. Under a strong gradient these displace cells by different amounts, and CPM's Potts neighbour-swapping sorts differentially- adhesive cells in a way the vertex topology resists -- so the spatial outcome genuinely depends on the substrate.
purpose.expected_outcome: Cross-backend spatial agreement well below the same-backend baseline; the TOST REJECTS equivalence.

key_assumptions: Mechanics-only (no rules/ODE/immune) so nothing shared forces agreement; the knobs are deliberately strong to enter a mechanics-dominated regime.
Nothing is tuned to hit a target; the study reports whatever the TOST returns (it rejected).
Same spatial metric + TOST + margin as crossparadigm-equivalence, so the two verdicts are directly comparable.

limitations: REVIEW: an artificial mechanics-only regime with a strong gradient + differential adhesion -- it shows the test has POWER but cannot establish sensitivity to realistic influenza-relevant discrepancies.

Replicates are now stochastic in their mechanics (mechanics_seed = rules_seed); power should still be mapped by graded injected deviations (effect-size sweep) and a matched-physical-response control (Stage 4 / BP-06, BP-07).
The cause of the remaining divergence (sorting / positional dynamics) is not yet isolated; the earlier migration-direction explanation is retired.
Mechanics-only, so fate is static; the divergence is spatial/positional by construction.
Demonstrates the test's POWER and that mechanics-driven outcomes are substrate-sensitive; it does not quantify a biological effect size.

report.title: A mechanics-dominated regime where the substrates still DIVERGE (test has power)
report.verdict: RE-RUN (2026-10-28). With the revised, calibrated vertex substrate and mechanics-stochastic replicates, spatial equivalence is still REJECTED (cross 0.417 vs same 0.775, diff +0.358 vs margin 0.10), so this remains a valid positive control for crossparadigm-equivalence. The earlier mechanism (vertex A cells climbing the gradient to y~17.9) came from the old uncalibrated vertex chemotaxis and is retired. With drift calibrated to the CPM, neither substrate moves A far (CPM y 11.0 -> 11.0, vertex 10.7 -> 10.1). The residual divergence is positional / sorting dynamics and still needs causal isolation.
report.main_insight: The equivalence test is not rigged to say "equivalent". But a positive control is only as good as its mechanics: part of the old divergence was a calibration artifact, not a substrate property.
report.caveat: An engineered extreme; mechanics-only (fate static); 3 seeds; cause of the remaining divergence not isolated.

findings.statement: On the calibrated vertex substrate with stochastic replicates, the spatial TOST still rejects (cross 0.417 vs same 0.775, diff +0.358), but not because of directed migration: neither substrate moves type A far up the gradient.

findings.explanation: Differential-adhesion sorting / positional dynamics differ between lattice Metropolis and vertex T1 rearrangement; not yet isolated.
findings.next_action: sweep adhesion contrast and gradient strength to map where equivalence breaks (BP-06/BP-07)

findings.statement: SUPERSEDED by F2 (2026-10-28): the vertex up-gradient climb was produced by the old, uncalibrated linear ActiveMigration mapping. In a mechanics-dominated regime the spatial equivalence TOST REJECTS (cross 0.20 vs same 1.00, diff +0.80 vs margin 0.10), driven by a directed migration difference (vertex A to y~17.9, CPM A to y~10.7). The equivalence test can detect a real substrate difference, so crossparadigm-equivalence's positive verdict is informative, not an insensitivity artifact.
